{{Short description|Number group/set}}
{{Orphan|date=July 2022}}
In mathematics, '''Gottlieb polynomials''' are a family of discrete [[orthogonal polynomials]] given by

:<math>\displaystyle \ell_n(x,\lambda) = e^{-n\lambda}\sum_k(1-e^\lambda)^k\binom{n}{k}\binom{x}{k} =e^{-n\lambda}{}_2F_1(-n,-x;1;1-e^\lambda)</math>

<ref>{{cite journal| last1=Gottlieb | first1=M. J. | year=1938 | title=Concerning some polynomials orthogonal on a finite or enumerable set of points. | journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] | issn=0002-9327 | volume=60 | issue=2 | pages=453–458 | doi=10.2307/2371307 | jfm=64.0329.01 | jstor=2371307 }}</ref>
